title: Multi-stream traffic reservoir and stability prober for phased upgrades
creator: Javier Morales
description: We need a holistic release guard for LTS and non-LTS channel upgrades that combines reserved traffic capacity (traffic reservoir), synthetic stability probing, and an automated gate that decides ramping or rollback based on SLO and error budget signals. This ticket implements the control-plane components and the runtime hooks required to run multi-stream phased upgrades safely across Dedicated and Private deployments.
background: Current progressive delivery primitives rely on simple percentage ramps and heuristic rollback thresholds. Past incidents showed slow detection of regressions in tails (p99 p999 latency) and difficulty allocating burst capacity for canaries without disturbing production SLOs. We also lack a reliable synthetic prober to exercise failure modes unique to certain models (large context, KV cache warmup).
goals: Introduce a traffic reservoir concept: a small, reserved pool of requests (synthetic + low-risk customer cohorts) that can be directed to new versions for fast validation without affecting baseline SLOs.

Implement a stability prober service that continuously sends workload-shaped synthetic requests to candidate versions and reports feature-specific metrics (cache-warmup ratio, token-generation latency distribution, hallucination proxy signals).
Build a gate controller that evaluates multiple signals (SLOs, probe health, infra metrics, cost delta) and returns an atomic decision: HOLD / RAMP_TO(X%) / ROLLBACK.
Provide a rollout policy DSL allowing product owners to express channel policies (LTS vs edge), minimum canary duration, and accepted regressions per-metric.
Integrate with console to visualize reservoir usage, probe results, and decision timelines for audits and postmortems.
Fail-safe: ensure immediate automatic fallback to a pinned LTS model if a critical threshold is crossed.
acceptance_criteria: Control-plane components deployable to staging and can be toggled via feature flag
Stability prober runs workload-shaped synthetic traffic and reports at least p50/p95/p99 latency, token error rate, and cache-warmup completion within 10s for 95% of probes
Gate controller can perform automated RAMP and ROLLBACK actions via existing rollout APIs
Traffic reservoir can be configured per-customer and isolated from baseline billing metrics
Console panel shows end-to-end timeline of decisions, probe health, and reservoir consumption
design_notes: See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RP/Multi-Stream+Reservoir+and+Prober. Key ideas: small separate routing namespace for reservoir traffic, synthetic request templates stored per-model, probe runners colocated in the same region for network parity, gate uses both absolute thresholds and relative delta to control sensitivity. Chosen thresholds must be parameterized per-model profile.
architecture_decisions: Reservoir is implemented as a separate routing shard with independent token/billing attribution to avoid distorting customer metrics
Prober will be a stateless k8s deployment with horizontal autoscaler relying on historical probe latency
Gate controller will be a separate microservice that consumes telemetry from the metrics pipeline and writes decisions to the rollout API using adaptive smoothing to avoid flip-flop
Rollbacks are executed by invoking the existing release orchestrator; immediate rollback path must be less than 30s to complete route changes under normal control-plane load
implementation_plan: 1) Schema: extend rollout API to support 'reservoir' targets and 'probe' tags (PR: github.com/redwood/release-api/pull/1123)
2) Prober service: implement probe templates, runners, and lightweight evaluation hooks (PR: github.com/redwood/prober/pull/45)
3) Gate controller: implement multi-signal evaluator, smoothing, and decision history store (PR: github.com/redwood/gate-controller/pull/78)
4) Runtime hooks: integrate routing changes + reservoir sharding into serving runtime (ENG runtime PRs linked below)
5) Console: add panels and audit export for approval traces and decisions
6) Staging run: test against canary models and run chaos tests (network latency, CPU pressure)
7) Gradual rollout to customers with LTS channel opt-in

risks: Reservoir leaks causing billing/metrics distortion if not properly isolated
False negatives: probe suite may not surface subtle quality regressions in hallucination
Flip-flop decisions if smoothing window misconfigured leading to oscillating rollouts
Operational complexity for customers with hybrid Dedicated/Private setups
mitigations: Isolate billing dimensions for reservoir traffic and run a 2-week accounting audit before GA
Iteratively expand probe templates and add ensemble detection heuristics for hallucination proxies
Add hysteresis and minimum decision intervals to gate controller; manual override via console
Provide a migration playbook and a compatibility test harness for Private deployments
monitoring_and_alerting: Gate controller emits decision events to the audit log and creates Prometheus metrics: gate_decisions_total{decision="ROLLBACK"}, gate_latency_seconds, reservoir_fill_ratio. Alerts: P1 if auto-rollback triggers in >3 deployments in 24h, P0 if rollback fails to complete within 60s.
rollback_algorithm_summary: Score = w1*delta_p99 + w2*error_rate_delta + w3*probe_failure_rate + w4*infrastructure_alert_score. We evaluate absolute and relative thresholds. If Score > critical_threshold -> immediate ROLLBACK. If Score in [warn,critical] -> HOLD and escalate to human for manual decision after 15 min. We use exponential smoothing on metric deltas to avoid reacting to single-sample noise.
rollout_policy_dsl_example:
channel: LTS
min_canary_duration: 30m
reservoir_percentage: 0.5
stability_probe_profile: large-context-read
max_accepted_p99_regression_ms: 200
actions:
  - condition: probe_failure_rate > 0.02
    action: ROLLBACK
  - condition: sustained_p99_delta > 150 for 10m
    action: HOLD
qa_plan: 1) Run prober suite against a control release and a synthetic degraded release. 2) Run chaos experiments that simulate KV cache misses and verify probe catches degradation. 3) Run canary ramps with reservoir enabled and validate metrics recorded and decisions taken as expected.
security_and_compliance_notes: Prober templates must not include any real customer data. All probe results stored with redaction and a TTL of 90 days. Private deployments default to disabled; customers must opt-in. KMS usage for decision audit export enabled.
console_changes: New tab 'Reservoir & Probes' showing: current reservoir utilization, per-probe health, decision timeline, ability to 'pause' gate or force a manual rollback. Audit export to S3 for compliance.
customer_migration_notes: For LTS customers, provide a one-click opt-in to use reservoir-based promotion. For private deployments, provide an on-prem prober binary and a gating shim that speaks to the local rollout controller.
